$comment: Machine-readable statement of this repo's hard gates, for agents and skills
that write code here. CLAUDE.md is the prose version and stays authoritative
for humans; this file is the part a tool can parse BEFORE editing.
Why it exists: a portable third-party skill knows design, or testing, or
security — it cannot know that adding one English string here without also
translating it into 13 locales and regenerating the type tree blocks the
commit. That gap produced two blocking violations in a single evaluation
run. Everything below was verified against package.json / lefthook.yml /
eslint.config.js rather than transcribed from prose.
Keep in sync when a gate changes. `npm run check` is the umbrella.
$readBeforeEditingCaveat: CATALOG.md is on this list because CLAUDE.md mandates it, but it is GENERATED and two of its
rows are known-wrong: `LoadingSpinner` is described as 'Canonical loading spinner… Use for any
full-element loading state' when the component renders null, and `DataGrid` reads 'CSS grid
fraction, e.' (a truncated fragment of an unrelated prop comment, because DataGrid has no
@catalog tag). Regenerating does NOT fix the LoadingSpinner row — that string is hardcoded in
the CURATED map at scripts/docs/gen-shared-catalog.mjs:56, which takes priority over any tag.
Prefer the `situationalDoctrine` map below and `uiRules.reuse.doNotHandRoll` over the catalog

situationalDoctrine.$comment: Read the named doc BEFORE writing the surface. These are the per-situation golden paths; each states one way, its mandated primitives, its anti-patterns, and the gate it is owed. Loading is deliberately TWO entries because the two situations have opposite prescriptions.
situationalDoctrine.a surface loading its data (tab/page/pan: docs/design/overview-loading.md (the five laws — root doctrine) + docs/concepts/golden-paths/page-loading.md (the applied path)
situationalDoctrine.theOneRuleThatSpansTwoOfThem: Spinners are BANNED for surfaces and REQUIRED for actions. feedback/LoadingSpinner satisfies neither — it renders null.

blockingGates.note: Clean on master. Errors on a branch are regressions from that branch.
0 errors required. ~10k warnings are a known, deliberate migration baseline — do not bulk-fix, but do not add to them either.
THE most common trip-up for tools that add UI strings. Adding a key to en.json without translating all 13 other locales fails the commit.
contracts + tiers + typecheck + lint + themes + tauri-configs + error-registry

--workspace AND --features desktop are both load-bearing. Without --features desktop the tauri build script aborts on the updater capability before compiling anything; without --workspace only the root package is linted.

NEVER bare `cargo test` on Windows - the lib unit-test binary carries no comctl32-v6 manifest and dies in the loader with exit 127 (0xc0000139) before main(). npm run test:rust embeds it post-link. npm run test:rust:crates narrows to core/db/engine.

97 of the 201 census rules target src-tauri. A baseline fails on a RISE and also on a silent DROP; `floor` catches a matcher that broke rather than a codebase that got clean. Ratchet with `npm run census -- --update` only when you can explain the movement.

Reports 14 unaddressed RUSTSEC advisories as of 2026-08-20. This gate was silently broken until then - the config carried a key cargo-deny 0.17 removed, so it exited on a deserialization error instead of checking anything.

codegenTriggers.when: you add or change any key in src/i18n/locales/en.json
codegenTriggers.note: Without this, t.section.key does not exist on the generated type and tsc fails. predev/prebuild do it automatically; a mid-session edit does not.

codegenTriggers.when: you add #[derive(TS)] #[ts(export)] to a Rust struct/enum
codegenTriggers.note: --workspace and --features desktop are BOTH required; without them ZERO bindings regenerate, and a run that produces no diff is indistinguishable from one that was already up to date. CI fails on `git diff --quiet src/lib/bindings/`. On a box where the test binary cannot launch (STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND), hand-edit the binding and say so in the PR.

codegenTriggers.when: you add a new Tauri command
you add or remove a component in src/features/shared/components/
codegenTriggers.note: Convenience, not a gate — a stale catalog no longer fails npm run check.

strings.rule: Every user-facing string goes through `const { t, tx } = useTranslation()` and `t.<section>.<key>`. Never hardcode English in JSX, placeholder, title, or aria-label.
addKeyWorkflow: write .i18n-work/missing-<locale>.json for all 13 non-English locales, preserving {placeholders}
strings.plurals: Suffix `_one` / `_other` and select the variant at the call site; both must carry {count}.

color.rule: Paint only through semantic tokens. No raw hex, no `text-white/*`, no `bg-white/*`.

contrast.rule: Body text uses bare `text-foreground`. Opacity below ~85% (`text-foreground/55`) and `text-muted-foreground` are both rejected — for hierarchy use `text-primary`, not lower opacity.
contrast.note: Matching neighbouring files is NOT sufficient here: ~10k existing warnings mean the incumbent code often violates this. New code must not inherit it.

radius.rule: Use semantic radii: rounded-{interactive,input,card,modal}. The numeric scale defines them; do not use it directly.

spacing.rule: Spacing tokens — hard-coded padding/gap opts the surface out of the user's density setting (data-density on <html>).

typography.rule: typo-* classes, not raw text-* sizes. Arbitrary values like text-[10px] are drift.

themes.rule: Every surface must survive a runtime theme switch. Light overrides go through [data-theme^="light"].

rtl.rule: Arabic ships. Do not assume English string lengths or left-to-right layout.

modals.rule: Use modals/BaseModal or feedback/ConfirmDialog. Never hand-roll a `fixed inset-0` backdrop.

reuse.rule: Check src/features/shared/components/CATALOG.md before building any UI primitive. ~115 exist.
reuse.$comment: doNotHandRoll was a bare string list with no primitive named and no gate declared, so a tool could read the ban and still not know what to import or whether anything would catch it. Each entry is now an object: `use` names the real component (verified against src/features/shared/components/ on 2026-08-13), `enforcedBy` names a rule that exists TODAY, and `gateOwed` records a gate a golden path has specified but nobody has built. Absent `enforcedBy` means UNENFORCED — every violation of that row ships under a green `npm run check`.

doNotHandRoll.use: feedback/ScenarioEmptyState (default export; imported as EmptyState). Chart panel: display/ChartEmptyState. Compact generic: display/EmptyIllustration.
doNotHandRoll.note: There is NO feedback/EmptyState — that path appeared in CLAUDE.md, Design.md and the reuse doc until 2026-08-13 and never existed. 12 feature-local *EmptyState components grew in the gap.

doNotHandRoll.use: buttons/Button (variant + size; aria-label on icon-* sizes)
doNotHandRoll.gateOwed: custom/prefer-button-primitive — specified in docs/concepts/golden-paths/button.md §9 (messageIds: unnamedControl, unthemedFocus, variantClone). 2,311 drift elements / 915 files, 844 with no accessible name at all.

doNotHandRoll.use: buttons/AsyncButton with an onClick that RETURNS the promise
doNotHandRoll.note: onClick={() => void fn()} returns undefined, which silently disarms both the guard and the self-derived spinner. 177 void handlers exist.
doNotHandRoll.gateOwed: custom/no-noop-busy-state messageId voidDisarmsGuard — specified in docs/concepts/golden-paths/inline-busy-state.md; autofixable, 34 hits, precision 100%.

doNotHandRoll.what: busy state on an action control
doNotHandRoll.use: buttons/AsyncButton (renders a real spinner) — NEVER feedback/LoadingSpinner
doNotHandRoll.note: feedback/LoadingSpinner renders null (LoadingSpinner.tsx:12-21). Spinners are banned for SURFACES and required for ACTIONS; see docs/design/overview-loading.md and docs/concepts/golden-paths/inline-busy-state.md.
doNotHandRoll.gateOwed: custom/no-noop-busy-state messageId noopSpinner — 252 call sites, structurally zero false positives (the component cannot render anything).

doNotHandRoll.use: display/UnifiedTable with isLoading + data for lists; layout/RouteChunkSkeleton as a lazy-route Suspense fallback; otherwise a calm delayed ghost per docs/design/overview-loading.md §C
doNotHandRoll.note: Never a spinner, never animate-pulse, never `if (loading) return <X/>` around chrome.
doNotHandRoll.gateOwed: none specified yet. Zero automated enforcement of the five laws; UnifiedTable has no test file.
custom/prefer-unified-table — specified in docs/concepts/golden-paths/tables.md §Gaps 9; role="columnheader" is the near-perfect signal (6 files, 4 true positives).

errors.rule: `toastCatch()` for user-facing, `silentCatch()` for background. Never an empty catch {}.

state.rule: Zustand slices with `useShallow` for selective subscriptions.

effects.rule: Clean up listeners, timers and subscriptions.

$comment: The backend is a 5-crate cargo workspace under src-tauri/: core (no Personas dep) -> db -> engine -> personas-desktop (app_lib), plus the macros proc-macro crate.
`crate::db` IS `personas_db` and `crate::error` IS `personas_core::error` (src/lib.rs:12,18) - re-exports, not separate layers.
Measured 2026-08-20 during the rust-refactor campaign. Full plan: docs/plans/rust-refactor.md (local, docs/plans is gitignored).

placement.rule: Put a module in the LOWEST crate whose reach closes. Anything touching AppState, AppHandle, tauri::, notifications, tray or a command entry point belongs in app_lib and nowhere else.
placement.note: Cargo enforces acyclicity for free - a path-dependency cycle fails resolution before anything compiles. What is NOT enforced is placement, and src/engine/mod.rs re-exports four crates into one namespace, so a call site cannot tell which crate it reached.

errors.rule: Every #[tauri::command] returns Result<T, AppError>. Pick the variant that names the failure's CAUSE (Auth, NetworkOffline, RateLimited, Forbidden, NotFound, ProcessSpawn, Validation). Reach for Internal/External only for text you genuinely do not control, and then put the operation in the message.
errors.note: 1,614 of 1,655 commands already comply, so the error type is NOT the debt. The payload is: ~100 commands return an untyped serde_json::Value, and 387 sites collapse a real cause into AppError::Internal(format!(..)).

commands.rule: A command is an adapter: validate, make ONE call into engine or repo, map the result. A body over ~40 lines is a service function sitting in the wrong file.
commands.returnType: a named #[derive(Serialize, TS)] #[ts(export)] struct - never serde_json::Value
commands.sync: A sync command must not touch rusqlite; that blocks the IPC worker. Use an async command over spawn_blocking, or an async repo call.
exemplars: src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/commands.rs (structure only - its Result<_, String> is the exception, not the model)

database.rule: A repo fn is `pub fn verb_noun(pool: &DbPool, ...) -> Result<T, AppError>` in db/src/repos/<area>/<table>.rs. A get-by-id returns Result<Option<T>> so it can say 'no such row'.
database.transactions: A write that must be atomic with another write gets a `pub(crate) fn verb_noun_in(tx: &Transaction<'_>, ...)` inner fn, and the pool fn opens the transaction. Use transaction_with_behavior(Immediate) whenever a read informs a write - a deferred transaction fails SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT in 0ms and ignores busy_timeout.
database.rowMapping: const COLUMNS plus the row_mapper! macro (db/src/macros.rs). Never SELECT * and never positional row.get(0) - together they mean any mid-table ADD COLUMN silently shifts every index.

concurrency.rule: Every spawn decides who waits: keep the JoinHandle and surface is_panic(), or run under catch_unwind with a durable write.
never: a perpetual loop with no stop path
a bare tokio::time::sleep as a loop's only wait
caching a Result in a OnceLock - it freezes the first attempt's failure for the life of the process
concurrency.loops: Implement ReactiveSubscription (src/engine/subscription.rs:69, 41 impls) or race the wait against a shutdown token inside tokio::select!.

panics.rule: No .unwrap() or .expect() in production code. Three exceptions: a static initialiser over a literal, a lock whose poisoning is deliberately treated as a panic report, and a documented invariant carrying an `// INVARIANT:` comment on the line above.
panics.tests: Tests may unwrap freely - clippy.toml sets allow-unwrap-in-tests.

sharedPrimitives.$comment: This backend's dominant defect is not missing abstractions, it is unadopted ones. Reach for these before writing your own. A NEW shared primitive must retire at least three hand-rolled copies in the same change - primitives built ahead of their callers is how this repo ended up with run_lanes at zero callers and acquire_logged under #[allow(dead_code)].
sharedPrimitives.subprocess: personas_engine::cli_process - the one place env scrubbing, timeout, PID registration and cancellation live
sharedPrimitives.poolAccess: acquire_logged(pool, label) (src-tauri/db/src/lib.rs:113) - carries the starvation instrumentation a bare pool.get() does not
sharedPrimitives.panicMessage: the shared panic-payload decoder - do not paste another copy of extract_panic_message
sharedPrimitives.events: emit_event plus the event_names! registry (src-tauri/core/src/events.rs) - never an inline json! payload under an unregistered name

testing.rule: Get the database from personas_db::init_test_db() / init_test_user_db(). Never write CREATE TABLE in a test - a hand-built fixture is not the production schema, and a self-opened Connection has foreign_keys OFF.
testing.run: npm run test:rust (whole workspace) or npm run test:rust:crates (core/db/engine only)

gitDiscipline.rule: Multiple CLI sessions share this checkout concurrently.
never: git stash — it sweeps other sessions' in-flight work, including untracked files
git add -A / git add . / git add -u — stage explicit paths only
always: read .claude/active-runs.md at session start; append your entry
classify every line of `git status --porcelain` as yours / pre-existing / another session's
after `git add` and BEFORE `git commit`, run `git diff --cached --stat` and confirm the file count matches what you staged
commit atomically per task; never hold >30 minutes of uncommitted work

commit through an isolated index when a sibling session is active: IDX=$(mktemp); GIT_INDEX_FILE=$IDX git read-tree HEAD; GIT_INDEX_FILE=$IDX git add <paths>; GIT_INDEX_FILE=$IDX git commit. Seed it with read-tree, NEVER with `cp .git/index` - the copy inherits staleness and silently records your own previous commit's files as deleted.

verify `git log --oneline -1` is YOUR message after every commit. Both `git commit -- <paths>` and `git commit --only <paths>` commit the WORKING TREE rather than the index, so a sibling's unstaged edit inside your pathspec rides in under your message.

docsSync.rule: A turn that changes user-visible behaviour must update every coupled surface in the same turn.
docsSync.dismissal: If the change is internal-only, say so in one sentence. Do not ignore silently.
